e: Telegram Bookmark Save any link, file, screenshot, page or video to your own Telegram group, sorted into topics.
x: Telegram Bookmark # Save any link, file, screenshot, page or video to your own Telegram group, sorted into topics. Telegram becomes your bookmark manager, with search, sync across all your devices, and no extra account. Version: 2.0.0 Developed by: asrbmy and linkwithiq Websites: asrbmy.github.io · linkwithiq.github.io Source code: github.com/asrbmy/telegram-bookmark Table of contents # How it works What is in the download Install the extension Set up Telegram Using the popup Save modes in detail Right-click menu and keyboard shortcut Automatic topic detection and site rules Duplicate warning History Multiple groups (profiles) Settings reference The download helper (YouTube and more) Privacy and security Limits Troubleshooting For developers Credits 1. How it works # text Copy Browser extension ──► Telegram Bot API ──► Your group (Topics on) (popup, menu, ├─ 🎬 Videos shortcut) ├─ 🎵 Music ├─ 🌐 Websites ├─ 📄 Documents ├─ 🖼️ Images └─ 📌 Read later You create a Telegram bot and a group with Topics turned on . Each topic is a category. The extension sends your saves through the bot to the right topic. Optionally, a small helper program on your own computer downloads videos and music (for example from YouTube) with yt-dlp and uploads them to the same topic. Everything runs on your own devices. There is no server owned by the developers and no analytics. 2. What is in the download # File Purpose telegram-bookmark-chrome.zip Extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers (Manifest V3) telegram-bookmark-firefox.zip Extension for Firefox (Manifest V2) telegram-bookmark-helper.zip Optional helper for video and audio downloads ( server.py + README) 3. Install the extension # Chrome, Edge, Brave # Extract telegram-bookmark-chrome.zip into a folder. Open chrome://extensions (Edge: edge://extensions ). Turn on Developer mode . Click Load unpacked and choose the extracted folder. Pin the extension from the puzzle-piece menu so the icon is always visible. Requires Chrome 110 or newer. Firefox # Extract telegram-bookmark-firefox.zip into a folder. Open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox . Click Load Temporary Add-on and select the file manifest.json (the file, not the folder or the zip). Firefox removes temporary add-ons when it closes, so repeat these steps next time. Your settings are kept. To keep it permanently, either: Upload the zip to addons.mozilla.org → Developer Hub → On your own , then install the signed .xpi it gives you, or Use Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly, set xpinstall.signatures.required to false in about:config , and install the zip. Requires Firefox 109 or newer. 4. Set up Telegram # You do this once. It takes about five minutes. Step 1: Create a bot # In Telegram, open @BotFather (it has a blue verified tick). Send /newbot . Choose a name, then a username ending in bot . Copy the token . It looks like 123456789:AAH-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx . Anyone with the token can control your bot. If it leaks, send /revoke to @BotFather. Step 2: Create the group # Create a new Telegram group. Telegram needs at least one other member to create it. You can remove them afterwards. Open the group, tap its name, tap Edit , and turn on Topics . Add your bot to the group. Open Administrators , add the bot, and turn on Manage Topics . Send any message in the group, for example "hello". Step 3: Connect the extension # Open the extension's Settings (the sliders icon in the popup). Go to Account and paste the Bot token . Click Find my group . The Group ID is filled in for you. It looks like -1001234567890 . If you are in several groups with the bot, you get a list to choose from. Click Test connection . You should see four green ticks: Bot is valid Group found Topics are enabled Bot is an admin and can manage topics Go to Topics and click Create missing topics in Telegram . The six default topics appear in your group. Settings save automatically. You will see a small "Saved" message at the bottom. Manual Group ID: open https://api.telegram.org/bot<YOUR_TOKEN>/getUpdates in your browser and look for "chat":{"id":-100... . Copy that number including the minus sign. 5. Using the popup # Click the extension icon on any web page. Area What it does Page card Shows the page icon, title and site name Duplicate banner Appears if you already saved this link (see section 9 ) Topic Chips for each category. The best match is selected automatically. Click another to change it Save as Link, File, Shot, Page, and (if the helper is on) Video and MP3 Note field Optional text or #tags . Press Enter to send. Your note is kept if you change topic Send to Telegram The main button. It changes to Send again when the link is a duplicate Save all N tabs Sends every open tab in this window (needs Advanced access) Group selector Top right. Appears when you have more than one profile Settings (sliders icon) Opens the settings window Save / History Switch between saving and your history at the bottom If the bot is not connected yet, the popup shows a Connect Telegram screen with a button that opens Settings. 6. Save modes in detail # Mode What is sent Notes Link A message with the page title, URL and your note Default. Telegram shows its normal link preview File The actual file (PDF, MP3, MP4, image, ZIP, etc.) uploaded as a document Needs Advanced access. Falls back to a link if the URL is a normal web page or the file is over 50 MB Shot A screenshot of the visible part of the page PNG. Sent as a photo, or as a document if it is over 9 MB or Telegram rejects it as a photo Page An HTML copy of the page, as a .html file Scripts are removed, a no-scripts security policy is added, and a base address is set so images and styles load when you open it online. It is not a fully offline archive Video Video downloaded by the helper (up to 720p MP4) Needs the helper MP3 Audio downloaded by the helper as MP3 Needs the helper and ffmpeg Text Your highlighted text plus the source title and link Used from the right-click menu when you select text Tabs All tabs in the window as a list Needs Advanced access. See below Automatic file mode. If Advanced access is on and the page address ends in a file type (pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, zip, mp3, m4a, mp4, jpg, png, webp, epub), the popup selects File for you. Otherwise it starts on Link . Save all tabs. All tabs go into one message (or a few, if the list is long) to stay within Telegram's rate limits. Link previews are turned off for this list, up to 200 tabs are sent, and the message starts with "📚 N tabs" and your note. Safe file downloads. The extension fetches files without your login cookies, stops after 120 seconds, refuses to read more than 50 MB, and blocks local and private network addresses (including after redirects). 7. Right-click menu and keyboard shortcut # Right-click menu # Right-click a page, link, image, video, audio file or selected text, then choose Save to Telegram : One entry per topic. Sends a link. If you right-clicked selected text (not on a link), it sends the text as a Text save with the source. ⬇️ Download file instead. Available on links, images, video and audio. Uses the automatic topic. 🎞 Download video (helper) and 🎧 Download audio (helper). Only shown when the helper is enabled. Keyboard shortcut # Alt + Shift + S saves the current page as a link to its automatically detected topic. Change it here: Chrome: chrome://extensions/shortcuts Edge: edge://extensions/shortcuts Firefox: Add-ons → gear icon → Manage Extension Shortcuts Badges # Saves from the right-click menu and the shortcut show a small badge on the toolbar icon for 2.5 seconds: Badge Meaning ✓ Sent ⬇ File uploaded … Helper download started = Skipped because it is a duplicate ! Error. Open the popup to see details 8. Automatic topic detection and site rules # The topic is chosen in this order: Your site rules (Settings → Site rules). Built-in detection: Detected Topic youtube.com, youtu.be, vimeo.com, dailymotion.com, twitch.tv Videos music.youtube.com, spotify.com, soundcloud.com, gaana.com, jiosaavn.com, music.apple.com Music .mp4 .mkv .webm .mov Videos .mp3 .m4a .wav .flac .ogg Music .pdf .doc(x) .xls(x) .ppt(x) .zip .epub Documents .jpg .png .gif .webp Images Everything else Websites If the detected topic does not exist in your profile, the first topic in your list is used. Site rules. In Settings → Site rules, type a website and pick a topic. A rule for github.com also covers gist.github.com and other subdomains. Rules apply to the popup, the right-click menu and the shortcut. A rule that points to a topic you deleted is ignored. 9. Duplicate warning # When you try to save a link that is already in your history, you get a warning instead of a second copy. Applies to Link, File, Page, Video and MP3 saves. Tracking parts are ignored when comparing: #fragments , utm_* , fbclid , gclid , igshid , and si . In the popup, the banner says when and where it was saved, and the button becomes Send again . Pressing it saves a duplicate on purpose. From the right-click menu and the shortcut, a duplicate is skipped and the badge shows = . Turn this off in Settings → Features. Duplicate checking needs history to be on. 10. History # Open the History tab in the popup. Search by title, link or note. Open a saved link in a new tab. Send again re-sends it as a link to the same topic. Shows the last 60 matches for the current group. In Settings → History you can Export JSON or Clear history . In Settings → Features you choose how many items to keep: 100, 300 or 1000. Turning history off stops it recording and also disables the duplicate warning. 11. Multiple groups (profiles) # Use a separate Telegram group for each area of life, for example Personal and Work. Each profile has its own bot token, Group ID, topics and history. Site rules and feature settings are shared by all profiles. Create, rename and delete profiles in Settings → Account. Switch profile with the selector at the top of the popup. The right-click menu follows the active profile. Site rules point to a topic by its internal key, so a rule only applies in profiles that contain that topic. 12. Settings reference # Account # Group profile, profile name, bot token (hidden, with a Show button), Group ID, Find my group , Test connection , New profile , Delete profile , and quick setup steps. Topics # Edit the icon , name and topic ID of each category. Add your own topics. Remove topics you do not want. Create missing topics in Telegram creates a forum topic for each category that has no ID yet. The group must have Topics turned on and the bot needs the Manage Topics right. Renaming a topic here does not rename it in Telegram. Rename it in Telegram too. If a category has no topic ID, saves go to the group's General topic. Site rules # Add, view and remove website → topic rules. Features # Setting What it does Advanced access Asks the browser for access to all websites. Needed to download files and to read all tabs for Save all tabs. Off by default Duplicate warning On or off Keep history On or off History size 100, 300 or 1000 items Keyboard shortcut Information on how to change it Helper # Enable the helper, set its address (default http://127.0.0.1:8765 ) and secret, and press Test helper to check that it runs and that yt-dlp and ffmpeg are installed. History # Export or clear your history. About # Version, developer credits, links, privacy summary. 13. The download helper (YouTube and more) # Browsers cannot download YouTube videos from inside an extension. The helper is a small Python program on your computer that does it with yt-dlp , which supports YouTube and over a thousand other sites. Install # Install Python 3.9 or newer. Run python -m pip install -U yt-dlp . Install ffmpeg . It is needed for MP3 and for joining video and audio. Extract telegram-bookmark-helper.zip and run python server.py . It prints a secret . In the extension go to Settings → Helper, turn the helper on, paste the secret and press Test helper . Use # In the popup, choose Video or MP3 and press Send. Or right-click a page or link → Save to Telegram → Download video (helper) or Download audio (helper) . The file appears in the chosen topic when it is ready. The popup only says the download has started. If a download fails, the bot posts a short reason and the link in the same topic. How it behaves # Video: up to 720p, MP4. Audio: MP3 at best quality. Only the single video, never a whole playlist. Up to 2 downloads run at the same time. Temporary files are deleted after each job. Videos are sent as videos and audio as audio. If Telegram refuses that, the file is sent as a document. Options # text Copy python server.py --port 8765 python server.py --secret MY_OWN_SECRET python server.py --max-mb 50 python server.py --api-base http://127.0.0.1:8081 --max-mb 1900 The secret can also come from the HELPER_SECRET environment variable. By default it is generated once and stored in ~/.telegram-bookmark-secret . Files over 50 MB # The public Telegram Bot API accepts uploads up to 50 MB. For files up to 2 GB, run your own Telegram Bot API server , log your bot out of the cloud API once with /logOut , then start the helper with --api-base and --max-mb 1900 as shown above. Helper security # Listens only on 127.0.0.1 . Requires the secret on every request. Rejects requests from web pages (browser Origin check) and from other host names (protects against DNS rebinding). Accepts only http and https links, validates the token and Group ID format, and limits the request size to 8 KB. Starts yt-dlp with an argument list, never through a shell, and passes the link after -- so it cannot be read as an option. Hides your bot token in any error message. Your bot token is sent only from the extension to the helper on your own computer, and from there to Telegram. 14. Privacy and security # What is stored # Everything is in your browser's local extension storage: profiles (token, Group ID, topics), site rules, settings and history. Nothing is synced to any developer server. The token is stored as plain text on your device, as is normal for extensions. Anyone with access to your browser profile could read it. Network connections # The extension connects only to: api.telegram.org to send your saves Your own helper at 127.0.0.1 or localhost , if you enable it A web address you choose to download, only when you use File mode with Advanced access on Permissions # Permission Why storage Save your settings and history contextMenus The right-click menu activeTab Read the current tab's title and address, take screenshots and copy the page when you click scripting (Chrome only) Copy the page HTML for the Page mode api.telegram.org , 127.0.0.1 , localhost Talk to Telegram and the helper All websites (optional) Requested only if you turn on Advanced access. Used for file downloads and Save all tabs Built-in protections # Only http and https links can be saved. javascript: , file: and browser pages are blocked. Telegram messages are sent as plain text, so page titles cannot inject formatting or links. File downloads block private and local addresses, send no cookies, and have size and time limits. All text from pages and Telegram is shown with safe DOM methods. No innerHTML is used. Background messages are accepted only from the extension's own pages. Strict content security policy for extension pages: script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'; base-uri 'none' . Saved page copies have scripts removed. Bot token and Group ID are checked against strict patterns before every request. 15. Limits # Item Limit Uploaded file size 50 MB (2 GB with a local Bot API server and the helper) Text message 4096 characters (the extension keeps to about 4000) Caption on a file, photo or screenshot 1024 characters (the extension keeps to 1000) Selected text 3000 characters Note 300 characters Save all tabs 200 tabs per click Telegram rate limits If Telegram says "too many requests", the extension waits and retries once File download time 120 seconds Screenshots Visible area only, not the whole page Page copy Needs the page to allow script injection. Browser pages and protected sites cannot be copied 16. Troubleshooting # Problem What to do Find my group says no group found Make sure the bot is in the group and is an admin. Send a new message in the group, then try again. If the bot has a webhook set, enter the Group ID manually "Invalid bot token" Copy the token again from @BotFather. Make sure there are no spaces. It must look like 123456789:AAH... "Group not found" Check the Group ID, including the minus sign. Make sure the bot is still a member "The bot needs admin rights" Make the bot an admin with the Manage Topics permission "Topics are off in this group" Open the group → Edit → turn on Topics "That topic no longer exists" You deleted the topic in Telegram. In Settings → Topics, clear its ID and press Create missing topics in Telegram Saves go to General The category has no topic ID. Press Create missing topics in Telegram or enter the ID by hand File button is greyed out Turn on Advanced access in Settings → Features File was sent as a link The address is a normal web page, not a downloadable file, or the file is over 50 MB "Downloads from local or private addresses are blocked" This is a safety feature. Download the file yourself and send it from Telegram "This page can't be copied" Browser pages (for example about: or chrome: ) and some protected sites cannot be read "Cannot reach the helper" Start server.py . Check the address in Settings → Helper "Wrong helper secret" Copy the secret printed by server.py into Settings → Helper again Helper download fails The bot posts the reason in the topic. Common causes: yt-dlp is out of date ( pip install -U yt-dlp ), ffmpeg is missing, or the file is over the size limit Shortcut does nothing Another extension may use the same keys. Change the shortcut in the browser's shortcut page Firefox extension disappeared Temporary add-ons are removed when Firefox closes. Load it again, or sign it for permanent use I changed the Firefox version and lost my settings The add-on ID changed in the rename. Enter the token and group again once 17. For developers # Layout # text Copy src/ ext.js Browser API shim, validation, URL helpers, topic detection dom.js Small DOM builder, icons, relative time store.js Storage, profiles, settings, duplicate lookup tg.js Telegram API client and all save modes background.js Context menu, shortcut, message handling, badges popup.html/.js/.css The popup options.html/.js/.css The settings window ui.css Shared design tokens and components icons/ 16, 32, 48, 128 px manifests/ chrome.json Manifest V3 (service worker) firefox.json Manifest V2 (background page) background.html Firefox background page helper/ server.py Download helper README.md Browser differences # Chrome / Edge / Brave Firefox Manifest V3 V2 Background Service worker Background page ( background.html ) Toolbar button action browser_action Page copy scripting.executeScript tabs.executeScript Optional all-sites access optional_host_permissions optional_permissions All code is shared. ext.js picks browser or chrome automatically. Data model ( storage.local ) # text Copy profiles: [{ id, name, token, chatId, cats: [{key,name,icon}], threads: {catKey: topicId} }] activeId: string rules: [{ host, catKey }] settings: { dupWarn, keepHistory, historyMax, helperEnabled, helperUrl, helperSecret } history: [{ id, ts, profileId, url, title, catKey, mode, note }] Add a save mode # Add the mode to the send() function in tg.js . Add a button in modes() in popup.js . If it can be duplicated, add it to the lists in findDup() ( store.js ) and in send() . 18. t: A Tour of the Writing Features
e: Diagrams, maths, videos, light and dark pictures, and glossary hints — everything you can put inside an article.
x: This article shows what you can add to a page beyond plain text. Every feature works with ordinary Markdown, and none of them needs a plugin. Diagrams # Write the diagram as text in a mermaid block and it is drawn for you, in the colours of the current theme. flowchart LR A[Write in Markdown] --> B[Upload the file] B --> C[GitHub builds the site] C --> D[Readers see it] Maths # Put a formula between dollar signs, such as , or on its own lines for a larger display: Prices like $5 and $10 stay as ordinary text. Videos # A video stays a plain button until you press it, so nothing is loaded from a video site by default. ▶ Big Buck Bunny — an open-source film Loads YouTube when you press play Pictures that follow the theme # If a picture named diagram-light.svg has a twin called diagram-light.dark.svg , the right one is shown in light or dark mode. Three steps from a file to a published page Hints for hard words # The first mention of a term from the glossary, such as Markdown or RSS, shows its meaning when you hover over it or tab to it.

t: Building Better Software: Notes, Research & Ideas
e: A collection of practical notes, research findings, and ideas for building better software, improving workflows, and staying curious.
x: Introduction # Good software doesn't happen by accident. It's the result of clear thinking, consistent practice, and a willingness to learn. In this article I'm sharing some notes, research insights, and ideas that help me build better software and work more effectively. These are not strict rules, but a personal collection of things that have been useful in real projects and day-to-day work. The goal is simple: learn, apply, and improve. Whether you're just starting out or have years of experience, there's always something new to explore. Technical Notes # Here are some technical notes that I keep coming back to. They cover tools, languages, and general development practices. Topic Tool / Language Key Takeaway Version Control Git Small, frequent commits make history easier to manage. Package Management npm / pip Use a lock file to keep builds consistent. Code Editor VS Code Extensions can save hours of repetitive work. Testing pytest Automated tests catch issues early and give confidence. Deployment GitHub Pages Static sites are simple, fast and reliable. Why small commits win # A commit that does one thing is easy to review, easy to revert and easy to explain six months later. If you struggle to write a short message for a commit, it is usually trying to do too much. Practical Examples # Here are a few small examples that I use in my projects. Feel free to adapt them to your own needs. 1. A simple Python script # This script reads a list of numbers and prints their average. python Copy numbers = [ 10 , 20 , 30 , 40 , 50 ] average = sum (numbers) / len (numbers) print ( f"Average: {average} " ) 2. A helpful Linux command # This command shows disk usage in a human-readable format. bash Copy df -h 3. Useful resources # Python Official Documentation — https://docs.python.org/ GitHub — https://github.com/ Mozilla Developer Network — https://developer.mozilla.org/ Frequently Asked Questions # How do I stay consistent with learning? Make it small and make it daily. Thirty focused minutes beat a weekend marathon that never gets repeated. Write down one thing you learned at the end of each session. What's the best way to organize notes? Pick one place and one convention, then stick with it. Plain Markdown files in a folder you can search are hard to beat. See how I take research notes for my setup. Which tools do you recommend for beginners? A good editor, Git, and one language you stay with long enough to build something real. The beginner's guide to Python is a gentle place to start. How can I improve my coding skills? Read other people's code, write small programs often, and get feedback. Rebuilding something that already exists is a surprisingly effective way to find the gaps in what you know.

t: Setting Up a Local Development Environment
e: A small, repeatable setup beats a clever one. Here is how I get a new machine ready for development without losing an afternoon.
x: A new laptop or a fresh clone should not take a day to become useful. The trick is to keep the setup small, write it down, and make it easy to check. Start with the smallest useful setup # You need four things on almost every project: an editor, a terminal, Git and the language runtime. Resist installing anything else until a project actually asks for it. Every extra tool is something to update and something that can break. Pin your tool versions # "Works on my machine" is usually a version mismatch. Record the runtime version in the repository so everyone, including future you, uses the same one. Node projects can use an .nvmrc file or the engines field in package.json . Python projects can use a .python-version file together with a virtual environment. Commit your lock file ( package-lock.json , poetry.lock , requirements.txt with pinned versions). Keep a setup script # If you do something twice, script it. A short script doubles as documentation: bash Copy #!/usr/bin/env bash set -euo pipefail node --version git --version npm ci npm test set -euo pipefail makes the script stop at the first problem instead of carrying on with a half-working environment. Check that it works # Finish every setup with one command that proves things are healthy: run the tests, build the project, or start the dev server and open it. A setup you have not verified is only a guess. Keep secrets out of the repository # Put credentials in environment variables or a local .env file, add that file to .gitignore , and commit an .env.example listing the names (not the values) that a newcomer needs to fill in.

e: Git tracks your changes on your own computer; GitHub is a place to share them. A short, practical tour of the everyday workflow.
x: People often use "Git" and "GitHub" as if they were the same thing. They are not, and knowing the difference makes everything else easier. Git versus GitHub # Git is a version control tool that runs on your computer. It records snapshots of your project, called commits, so you can see what changed, when, and why. GitHub is a website that hosts Git repositories. It adds collaboration features on top: pull requests, issues, and hosting such as GitHub Pages. The everyday loop # Most days you will repeat the same small cycle. bash Copy git status # what has changed? git add notes.md # stage the change git commit -m "Add notes on caching" git push # send it to GitHub Check git status often; it tells you exactly what Git thinks is going on. Branches # A branch is a separate line of work. Create one for each idea so the main branch always stays in a working state. bash Copy git switch -c fix-typo-in-readme # …edit files, commit… git push -u origin fix-typo-in-readme Pull requests # When a branch is ready, open a pull request on GitHub. It shows the difference, lets others comment, and merges the change when everyone is happy. Even on solo projects, reading your own pull request before merging catches surprising mistakes. Commands worth memorising # Command What it does git clone <url> Copy a repository to your computer git log --oneline Show a compact history git diff Show unstaged changes git restore <file> Discard changes in a file git pull Fetch and merge the latest changes Next steps # Once the loop feels natural, learn how to resolve a merge conflict and how to write a clear commit message. Those two skills cover most of the real-world friction.

e: Seven low-effort habits that reduce how much of your browsing is tracked, without turning the web into a chore.
x: You do not need to become a security expert to browse more privately. A handful of habits, applied consistently, do most of the work. 1. Keep your browser updated # Updates fix security holes that are actively exploited. Turn on automatic updates and restart the browser when it asks. 2. Use fewer extensions # Every extension can read the pages you visit. Keep only the ones you truly use, install them from the browser's official store, and remove anything you no longer remember adding. 3. Turn on HTTPS-only mode # Most modern browsers can refuse to load pages over plain HTTP, or at least warn you first. This stops anyone on the same network from reading or altering what you send. 4. Separate your activities with profiles # Use one browser profile for banking and important accounts, and another for casual browsing. Cookies and logins stay separate, so a tracker on a recipe site cannot see your other life. 5. Control cookies and trackers # Block third-party cookies, and consider clearing site data when you close the browser. Expect to sign in more often; that is the trade-off. 6. Use a password manager # Unique passwords for every site limit the damage when one service is breached. A manager also refuses to autofill on look-alike domains, which helps against phishing. 7. Think before you click "Sign in with…" # Social sign-in is convenient, but it ties your accounts together. For services you do not fully trust, create a separate account with its own email address. What these tips do not do # None of this makes you anonymous. Your internet provider, the sites you log in to, and your own habits all still reveal things. The aim is to reduce needless tracking, which is a reasonable goal even if perfect privacy is not. If you face a specific threat, read threat modelling for everyday people before choosing tools.

e: Variables, lists, loops and functions in one sitting, with small programs you can run and change.
x: Python is a good first language because it reads almost like plain English. This guide covers the handful of ideas you will use in nearly every program. Run your first script # Save the following as hello.py and run it with python hello.py : python Copy name = "world" print ( f"Hello, {name} !" ) The f before the quotes lets you place variables inside {} braces. Variables and types # A variable is a name for a value. Python figures out the type for you. python Copy age = 30 # int price = 19.99 # float language = "Python" # str is_ready = True # bool Lists and loops # A list holds several values in order. A for loop visits each one. python Copy scores = [ 72 , 88 , 95 , 64 ] for score in scores: if score >= 70 : print (score, "pass" ) else : print (score, "needs work" ) Indentation is not decoration in Python — it defines which lines belong to the loop or the if . Functions # Wrap steps you repeat in a function and give it a clear name. python Copy def average ( values ): return sum (values) / len (values) print (average([ 72 , 88 , 95 , 64 ])) Practise by changing things # Reading is not enough. Take each example above and change it: add a score, pass a different list to average , print a different message. When something breaks, read the error message from the bottom up; the last line usually names the problem. Where to go next # Learn dictionaries and how to read a file, then build something small that you would actually use, such as a script that renames photos or totals a spreadsheet column. The official tutorial at https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/ is thorough and free.

e: Plain Markdown files, one idea per note, and a weekly review. A note-taking system simple enough to keep using.
x: I have tried many note-taking apps. What lasted was not an app at all; it was a few habits and a folder of text files. Why plain text # Markdown files open anywhere, search instantly, and survive any software company going away. They also work nicely with Git, which gives me history for free. Two kinds of notes # I separate what a source says from what I think about it. Source notes summarise one paper, article or talk in my own words, with the reference at the top. Idea notes hold a single claim or question, written so I can understand it later without the source open. They link to the source notes that support them. A template for source notes # markdown Copy # Title of the source - Author / year: - Link: - Why I read it: ## Main claim One or two sentences. ## Evidence What they showed, and how strong it is. ## My questions What is missing or unclear? The "Why I read it" line matters most. Without it, notes turn into summaries nobody needs. Write in your own words # Copying a quote feels productive but teaches nothing. Restating a paragraph in a sentence forces you to find out whether you understood it. The weekly review # Once a week I spend twenty minutes reading the notes I made, linking related ideas and deleting anything I would not miss. This is where the connections appear, and it keeps the folder from becoming a pile. Keep it light # If a system needs more effort than the thinking it supports, simplify it. A rough note you actually wrote beats a perfect one you postponed.

e: A multi-pass approach to research papers that saves hours and helps you decide what deserves a close read.
x: A single research paper can take hours to read properly, and you rarely need that for every one. Reading in passes lets you stop as soon as you have what you need. Pass one: the five-minute skim # Read the title, abstract, introduction and conclusion. Glance at the headings and figures. Then ask: What problem does this paper address? What do the authors claim to have found? Is it relevant enough to read further? Many papers end here, and that is a good outcome. S. Keshav describes a three-pass method like this in his short article "How to Read a Paper"; it is worth reading in full. Pass two: follow the argument # Now read carefully, but skip the proofs and fine technical detail. Study the figures and tables: are the axes labelled, do the error bars exist, are the comparisons fair? Note references you want to follow up. Pass three: challenge it # Only for papers that matter to your work. Try to reconstruct the argument yourself and notice where you disagree. The aim is to understand the paper well enough to explain its weaknesses. Habits that help # Keep a list of questions before you start; reading with a purpose is faster. Write a three-sentence summary immediately afterwards, while it is fresh. Read the related-work section to learn the field, not just the paper. Accept that you will not understand everything on the first read. When to stop # If the second pass shows the paper is not useful, stop and move on. Finishing something just because you started it is a poor use of attention.

e: Why I publish half-finished thoughts, what it has taught me, and the small rules that keep it comfortable.
x: For a long time I kept my notes private because they were not good enough. Then I noticed that nothing I was saving was getting better either. What changed # Publishing sets a deadline and an audience, even a tiny one. Knowing someone might read a paragraph makes me check my facts, cut the waffle and finish the thought. That is most of the benefit, and it does not require many readers. The things I was afraid of # I worried about being wrong in public. It has happened, and it was fine. A correction, clearly marked, is more useful to readers than silence, and it is how I learned the most. I worried nobody would care. Mostly nobody does, at first, and that is freeing. You get time to find your voice before anyone expects one. Small rules I follow # Say what I know and how I know it. Label guesses as guesses. Add an "Updated" date when I change something important. Write for one specific person, usually past me. Link to the sources I used, so readers can check. Publish before it feels ready. A finished imperfect post beats a perfect draft. Writing as thinking # The surprise has been that writing is not only a way to share what I think. It is how I find out what I think. A fuzzy idea becomes clear the moment I try to put it in a sentence, and many ideas turn out not to survive that test. If you are hesitating # Start with something small: one useful thing you learned this week. Put a date on it, publish it, and write the next one. The habit matters more than any single post.

e: Before you pick a privacy tool, work out what you are protecting and from whom. A simple set of questions does most of the work.
x: Security advice often arrives as a long checklist. A checklist is not a plan, because it does not know what matters to you. A threat model is the plan: a short, honest answer to "what could go wrong, and how much do I care?" Five questions # Write a sentence or two for each. What do I want to protect? Photos, accounts, money, location, your identity? Who might want it? A stranger, an advertiser, a former partner, an employer? How likely is it? Be realistic about the common cases and the rare ones. How bad would it be if it happened? Embarrassing, expensive, dangerous? How much effort am I willing to spend? Protection that is too annoying will be abandoned. An example # Here is how the answers might look for an ordinary person with a few online accounts. Asset Who might want it Likelihood Impact Sensible response Email account Criminals running credential-stuffing attacks High High Unique password, two-factor authentication Browsing history Ad networks Very high Low Tracker blocking, separate profiles Family photos Cloud outages, lost phones Medium Medium Regular backups in two places Home address Data brokers Medium Medium Opt out where possible, share less What the table shows # The biggest risks are boring. Protecting your email account — the key that resets everything else — matters far more than exotic tools. Spend effort where likelihood and impact are both high, and relax about the rest. Revisit it # Your situation changes: a new job, a new relationship, a public project. Review your answers once a year or whenever something significant changes.
